messages:
alex: throwing out a concrete idea to reduce cross-tenant kv-warm interference: introduce 'shaping gardens' as a placement+shaping primitive. each garden groups queues by affinity (kv-warm, slab, region) and exposes a tiny admission surface: target_window_ms, max_tokens, headroom_pct.
mira: short take: gardens are placement/shaping, lanes remain QoS. why do we need gardens vs expanding lane semantics?
alex: lanes handle priority and fairness. gardens inform where to place batches and how to size windows for kernel/cache efficiency. helps avoid mixing cache-hot tenants into the same slab eviction domain.
sanjay: another surface increases ops complexity. who owns garden settings: runtime autotune or ops config?
carol: ops should not hand-tune per-customer by default. start with telemetry-driven rule defaults and an opt-in autotuner later.
alex: proposal for defaults: for cache-hot gardens pick target_window_ms = clamp(1.4 * p50_ms, 3ms, 50ms). cold gardens get wider windows. headroom_pct start conservative (6-12%).
infra-bot: deploy-bot: batcher v0.8.1 deployed to canary with shaping-gardens gate :rocket:
mira: we need a precise borrowing model across gardens. without it a hot garden could borrow shared headroom and starve others.
sanjay: tradeoff: strict isolation wastes HW, loose allows tail blowups. suggest a small global deficit pool (e.g., 5-10% of total headroom) and per-garden borrow cooldowns and repayment windows.
carol: observability requirements: record borrow events with origin/destination garden id, amount, and pre/post tail percentiles. sample traces for borrowed batches so SRE can triage quality regressions.
alex: rollout plan: gate behind runtime flag, start with two gardens (hot_local, shared_cold), expose garden panels in console (headroom, borrow_rate, tail latency). canary on Dedicated first.
mira: UX: make garden ids human-readable and log mapping to slab/gpu id. helps with quickgrep during incidents.
sanjay: for customers, keep auto-mode default; expert-mode exposes garden tuning to advanced customers.
carol: I'll add a 24h emulator fuzz test: bursty tenants + steady background, randomized hotspots, measure tail-latency and utilization to catch monopolization.
alex: next steps: (1) add garden metadata to placement layer, (2) implement borrow accounting + deficit pool, (3) emulator fuzz + dashboard, (4) canary and monitor. I'll open a short RFC with the runtime API and telemetry fields. tagging @sanjay @carol to follow up. :+1:
